title: Command-line tool quickly removes Apple Intelligence from macOS 27
gist: macOS 27 Golden Gate drops the toggle for disabling Apple Intelligence, so a developer released the open-source RemoveMacAI command-line tool to turn it off and delete the models. Its quick traction (1,700 GitHub stars) signals user pushback against bundled on-device AI.

insights.claim: macOS 27 Golden Gate has no toggle to turn off Apple Intelligence, unlike earlier macOS versions, so the on-device AI models occupy disk space even if users never use them.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Apple is making AI a non-optional default part of the OS, which raises the stakes for adoption metrics and user goodwill.
insights.locator: A new tool is allowing Mac users

insights.claim: Apple Intelligence models are said to take about 12GB by the developer's estimate, but can take over 30GB according to The Verge, a real storage cost on Macs.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Forced multi-GB model footprints are a hidden cost of on-device AI, especially on low-storage base Macs.
insights.locator: They said that Apple's Intelligence models

insights.claim: RemoveMacAI disables Siri, Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, the ChatGPT extension and summaries, deletes the models and blocks re-download, while Dictation keeps working as a separate setting.
insights.speaker: Om Lahore
insights.so_what: The ChatGPT extension being bundled and removable shows OpenAI's distribution on Apple devices can be switched off by users.

insights.claim: The tool works through a user-approved configuration profile and Apple's own asset service, so System Integrity Protection stays on and nothing in /System is modified, and it is reversible via a revert command.
insights.speaker: Om Lahore
insights.so_what: Apple's own management mechanisms enable the opt-out, so Apple can't easily block it without breaking enterprise-style controls.

insights.claim: RemoveMacAI reached 1,700 GitHub stars within about a week and Reddit users report it works, indicating real demand for opting out of Apple Intelligence.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Stars are a rough proxy for an aversion segment; a vocal minority, not proof of mass rejection.

insights.claim: The article reads interest in the tool as evidence that some users dislike some or all Apple Intelligence features, despite Apple's growing emphasis on AI-driven device and software upgrades.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A gap between Apple's AI-centred upgrade story and consumer appetite is a risk to AI-driven refresh-cycle narratives.

insights.claim: A Hacker News commenter likened macOS to Windows de-crufting, saying users now need third-party scripts on a fresh macOS install to regain control of system resources and remove unwanted crapware.
insights.speaker: Hacker News user
insights.so_what: Perceived bloat erodes Apple's premium 'it just works' positioning with power users.
insights.quote: you need to run third-party scripts on a new OS installation to gain back control of your system resources and remove unwanted crapware
insights.locator: Reminds me of all the de-crufting

insights.claim: Many users are happy to use Apple Intelligence, and the tool simply restores for the rest the degree of control Apple previously offered.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: The backlash is about choice rather than AI itself, so a silent majority may still adopt it.
